title: JwtHeader
description: The header of a JWT this provider issues, derived from identity_oidc::jwt::JwtHeader. `typ` carries #[serde(rename = "typ")] — the rename is a no-op against the wire name but is written out so the spelling is explicit and a reader does not have to know that `type` would have been the same. The `use` rename in the JWKS is NOT like this: that one changes the wire name, because the Rust field is `use_` (see json-web-key.schema.json).
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; no JWT is signed anywhere in the bootstrap phase

alg.description: The signing algorithm. RS256 only. Two constants exist on purpose — JwtHeader::ALGORITHM is what the provider emits, JwtHeader::ACCEPTED_ALGORITHM is what it verifies with, and they are separate so a future second algorithm cannot silently widen what is accepted. A single shared constant is how 'alg: none' gets accepted.

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is a String in Rust

typ.description: The token type, when the token is not an ID token. Declared values: 'JWT' (JwtHeader::TYPE_ID_TOKEN) and 'at+jwt' (JwtHeader::TYPE_ACCESS_TOKEN). Omitted when absent.

x-rename.note: the rename here does not change the wire name; it is recorded because the attribute is present and a reader should not assume every rename in this crate is load-bearing

x-accepted-values.constraining: the field is an Option<String> in Rust

kid.description: The key identifier — which key in the JWKS signed this. A JWT header naming a kid the JWKS does not carry is a verification failure, not a reason to try every key.

x-boundary-note: identity-oidc can write this header and can parse a JWK set. It cannot sign, verify, or check an expiry — there is no function in crates/identity-oidc/src/jwt.rs that takes a secret or a key, by construction. Anything in this file that implies a token is valid is a lie.
